  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:center;"><a href="#"></a><a id="notes" href="#"></a><b>DAILY JOURNAL CORPORATION</b> </p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> The Corporation and Operations</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Daily Journal Corporation publishes newspapers and websites covering California and Arizona and produces several specialized information services. It also serves as a newspaper representative specializing in public notice advertising (the &#8220;Traditional Business&#8221;). Daily Journal Corporation, along with its wholly owned subsidiaries, are referred to as the &#8220;Company&#8221; or &#8220;Daily Journal&#8221;.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Journal Technologies, Inc. (&#8220;Journal Technologies&#8221;), a wholly owned subsidiary of Daily Journal, supplies case management software systems and related products to courts, prosecutor and public defender offices, probation departments and other justice agencies, including administrative law organizations, city and county governments and bar associations. These organizations use the Journal Technologies family of products to help manage cases and information electronically, to interface with other critical justice partners and to extend electronic services to the public, including e-filing and a website to pay traffic citations and fees online. These products are licensed or subscribed to in approximately <em style="font: inherit;">37</em> states and internationally.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Essentially all of the Company&#8217;s U.S. operations are based in California and Utah. The Company also has a presence in Australia where Journal Technologies is working on <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> software installation projects and in British Columbia, Canada, where the Company operates a wholly-owned subsidiary, Journal Technologies (Canada), Inc.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Significant Accounting Policies</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145945881" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Basis of Presentation</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial information and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;). Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and footnotes required by GAAP for complete annual financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly owned and controlled subsidiaries. All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In the opinion of management, the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments, consisting only of normal and recurring adjustments, necessary for a fair presentation of the Company&#8217;s financial position as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and the results of operations and stockholders&#8217; equity for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em>&#160;months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. The results of operations for interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for the full fiscal year ending&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2026</em>&#160;or for any other interim period.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The condensed consolidated balance sheet as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;has been derived from the audited consolidated financial statements as of and for the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>&#160;included in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K. These interim financial statements should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and related notes included in that Annual Report.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" id="c145945882" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Concentrations of Credit Risk</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentration of credit risk consist of cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, marketable securities and accounts receivable. The Company&#8217;s cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash are held at financial institutions where account balances <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>typically exceed federally insured limits. The Company limits its exposure by primarily placing its cash in interest-bearing deposit accounts with high credit quality financial institutions and by purchasing&#160;marketable&#160;securities. Management believes the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exposed to significant credit risk due to the financial strength of the depository institutions in which the cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash are held. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk of loss.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c145945883" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Use of Estimates</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Estimates and assumptions made by management include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the estimated fair values of marketable securities, management incentive plans, equity awards, and the accounting for income taxes. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

Credit limits, setting and maintaining credit standards, and managing the overall quality of the credit portfolio is largely centralized. The level of credit is influenced by the customer&#8217;s credit and payment history which the Company monitors when establishing a reserve.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The change in accounts receivable, net, is as follows (in thousands):</p> <p style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchDevelopmentAndComputerSoftwarePolicyTextBlock" id="c145945887" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Journal Technologies</i>&#8217;<i> Software Development Costs</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Development costs related to software products for sale or licensing are expensed as incurred until the technological feasibility of the product has been established. Thereafter, until the product is released for sale, software development costs are capitalized and reported at the lower of unamortized cost or net realizable value of the related product. The establishment of technological feasibility and the ongoing assessment of recoverability of costs require considerable judgment by the Company with respect to certain internal and external factors, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, anticipated future product revenue, estimated economic life and changes in hardware and software technology.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">If there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> program design completed, technological feasibility is reached upon the completion of a working model.&#160; Capitalization of software development costs ceases, and amortization of capitalized software development costs (if any) commences when the products are available for general release. Under the Company&#8217;s software development life cycle policy and agile development methodology, technological feasibility is typically established when a working model has been completed and approved through internal quality assurance, which typically occurs late in the development cycle and near the time the software is ready for customer testing and release. As a result, the period between technological feasibility and general release is generally insignificant, and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> software development costs have been capitalized to date. Research and development expenses related to software development are approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943771" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseSoftwareExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943772" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseSoftwareExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively. Research and development expenses are approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943776" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseSoftwareExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943777" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseSoftwareExcludingAcquiredInProcessCost" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.    <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DiscontinuedOperationsPolicyTextBlock" id="c145945888" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Assets and Liabilities Held for Sale</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company classifies long&#8209;lived assets (or disposal groups) as held for sale in the period in which all required criteria are met. Upon designation as held for sale, the assets of the disposal group are presented separately in the consolidated balance sheets as assets held for sale.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Long-lived assets to be sold are classified as&#160;held for sale&#160;in the period in which they meet all the criteria for the disposal of long-lived assets. The Company measures assets&#160;held for sale&#160;at the lower of their carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell. During the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> the Company entered into agreements to sell a building and its related land in Los Angeles, California (collectively, the "Building"), which is held within the Traditional Business segment. Upon meeting the held for sale criteria, the Company ceased depreciation on the Building and determined that <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> adjustment to its $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943787" contextRef="i_2026-01-31_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DisposalGroupHeldForSaleOrDisposedOfBySaleNotDiscontinuedOperationsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AssetsOfDisposalGroupIncludingDiscontinuedOperation" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million carrying value was required. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>sales efforts are ongoing, and the Building continues to meet the held for sale criteria.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c145945889" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Income Taxes</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company accounts for income taxes using an asset and liability approach which requires the recognition of deferred tax liabilities and assets for the expected future consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts for financial reporting purposes and the tax basis of the assets and liabilities. The Company accounts for uncertainty in income taxes under Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> which prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement methodology to recognize and measure an income tax position taken, or expected to be taken, in a tax return. The evaluation of a tax position is based on a <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-step approach. The <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> step requires an entity to evaluate whether the tax position would &#8220;more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not&#8221;</em> be sustained upon examination by the appropriate taxing authority. The <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> step requires the tax position be measured at the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em> likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. In addition, previously recognized benefits from tax positions that <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer meet the new criteria would be derecognized.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c145945890" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Revenue Recognition</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company recognizes revenues in accordance with the provisions of Accounting Standard Update ("ASU") <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em>&#160;<i>Revenue from Contracts with Customers (ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em>)</i>. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> for further discussion and related disclosures regarding revenue recognition.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the Traditional Business, proceeds from the sale of subscriptions for newspapers, court rule books and other publications and other services are recorded as deferred revenue and are included in earned revenue only when the services are provided, generally over the subscription term. Advertising service fees and other revenues, which represent primarily agency commissions received from outside newspapers in which the advertising is placed, are recognized when advertisements are published and are recorded on a net basis.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Journal Technologies contracts <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include several products and services, which are generally distinct and include separate transaction pricing and performance obligations. These revenue contracts include (i) implementation consulting fees to configure the system to go-live, (ii) subscription software license, maintenance (including updates and upgrades) and support fees, and (iii) <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party hosting fees when used. For contracts containing multiple performance obligations, the Company allocates the transaction price on the basis of the relative standalone selling price of each distinct good or service, and utilizes the residual approach to estimate the standalone selling price of implementation consulting fees, whereby the standalone selling price is estimated by reference to the total transaction price less the sum of the observable standalone selling prices of its subscription software licenses, maintenance and support fees, and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party hosting fees. These contracts include assurance-type warranty provisions for limited periods and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include financing terms. For most contracts, the Company acts as a principal with respect to certain services, such as data conversion and interfaces. Hosting services are provided with support by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties, and the Company recognizes such revenues and related costs on a gross basis. The Company considers several factors to determine if it controls the good or service before it is transferred to the client and therefore is the principal. These factors include (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) if the Company has primary responsibility for fulfilling the promise and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) if the Company has discretion in establishing price for the specified good or service. For legacy contracts with perpetual license arrangements, licenses and consulting services are recognized at point of delivery, and maintenance revenues are recognized ratably after the go-live.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company issues invoices that have payment terms which require payment within <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days. Amounts that have been invoiced are recorded in accounts receivable and in deferred revenue or revenue, depending on whether the required performance services have been completed. Proceeds from subscription-type revenues, including circulation revenue, license, maintenance and support services, and hosting services, are deferred at the time of sale and are recognized on a pro-rata basis over the terms of the subscriptions or service period, and unearned proceeds are recognized within deferred subscriptions and deferred maintenance agreements and others in the consolidated balance sheets. Proceeds from consulting fees are recognized at point of delivery upon service completion, and unearned consulting fee proceeds are recorded under deferred revenue on the condensed consolidated balance sheets. Other public service fees are earned and recognized as revenues when the Company processes credit card payments on behalf of the courts via its websites through which the public can e-file cases and pay traffic citations and other fees.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

    </ix:exclude> <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> also requires the capitalization of certain costs of obtaining contracts, specifically sales commissions which are to be amortized over the expected term of the contracts. For its software contracts, the Company incurs an immaterial amount of sales commission costs which have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant impact on the Company&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations. In addition, the Company&#8217;s implementation and fulfillment costs do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet all criteria required for capitalization. As a result, there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> fulfillment costs that are capitalized for the software contracts.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Since the Company recognizes revenues when it can invoice the customer pursuant to the contract for the value of completed performance, as a practical expedient and because reliable estimates cannot be made, it has elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to include the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied performance obligations. These unallocated prices primarily relate to the eFile-it&#8482; and ePay-it&#8482; transactions for which service fees are collected and recognized when the Company processes credit card payments on behalf of the courts via its websites through which the public can e-file cases or pay traffic citations.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145945891" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Accounting Pronouncements <em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Yet Adopted</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>, which provides qualitative and quantitative updates to the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid disclosures, among others, in order to enhance the transparency of income tax disclosures, including consistent categories and greater disaggregation of information in the rate reconciliation and disaggregation by jurisdiction of income taxes paid. The amendments in <i>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em></i> are effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024, </em>or the Company&#8217;s fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> and subsequent interim periods, with early adoption permitted. The amendments should be applied prospectively; however, retrospective application is also permitted. The Company is currently in the process of reviewing the guidance and evaluating its impact on its consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;<i>Income Statement </i>&#8211;<i> Reporting Comprehensive Income </i>&#8211;&#160;<i>Expense</i>&#160;<i>Disaggregation</i>&#160;<i>Disclosures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>):</i>&#160;<i>Disaggregation</i>&#160;<i>of Income Statement</i>&#160;<i>Expenses</i>, which requires additional disclosure of certain amounts included in the&#160;expense&#160;captions presented on the statement of operations, as well as disclosures about selling&#160;expenses. ASU&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em></i>-<i><em style="font: inherit;">03</em></i>&#160;is effective for fiscal years beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026</em><i>,</i>&#160;or the Company&#8217;s fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2028</em><i>,</i>&#160;and subsequent interim periods, with early adoption permitted.&#160; Early adoption is permitted for annual financial statements that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;yet&#160;been issued. The Company is evaluating the disclosure requirements related to the new standard.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em>&#160;<i>Intangibles</i>&#8212;<i>Goodwill and Other</i>&#8212;<i>Internal-Use Software (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">350</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>)</i>, which modernizes the accounting guidance for internal-use&#160;software costs&#160;by eliminating the requirement to assess software development stages and introduces a new capitalization threshold. ASU&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em></i>-<i><em style="font: inherit;">06</em></i>&#160;is effective for fiscal years beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027</em><i>,</i>&#160;or the Company&#8217;s fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2029</em><i>,</i>&#160;and subsequent interim periods, with early adoption permitted.&#160; Early adoption is permitted for annual financial statements that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;yet&#160;been issued. The Company is currently in the process of reviewing the guidance and evaluating its impact on its consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>New Accounting Pronouncements Adopted</i> </p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> new accounting standards adopted during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943887" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="djco:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognizedDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145943889" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="djco:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognizedDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">14.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in revenue, respectively, were recognized from deferred revenue at the start of each period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <div></div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3202821" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">4.</em> Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s financial instruments include marketable securities that are measured at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company&#8217;s holdings of marketable securities were concentrated in just <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> companies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Fair value is based on the price that would be received from selling an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Fair value is estimated by applying the following hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels and bases the categorization within the hierarchy upon the lowest level of input that is available and significant to the fair value measurement:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table style="border-collapse:collapse;height:auto;width:100%;"><tbody><tr><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8212;&#160;defined as observable inputs based on unadjusted quoted prices for identical instruments in active markets;</p></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table style="border-collapse:collapse;height:auto;width:100%;"><tbody><tr><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8212;&#160;defined as inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> that are either directly or indirectly observable in the marketplace for identical or similar instruments in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active; and</p></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table style="border-collapse:collapse;height:auto;width:100%;"><tbody><tr><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p></td><td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8212;&#160;defined as unobservable inputs in which little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data exists where valuations are derived from techniques in which <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more significant inputs are unobservable.</p></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company determines the level in the fair value hierarchy within which each fair value measurement falls in its entirety, based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety. In determining the appropriate levels, the Company performs an analysis of the assets and liabilities at each reporting period end.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The carrying amounts of cash,&#160;restricted cash, accounts receivable, accrued liabilities and accounts payable approximate fair value because of the short maturity and high liquidity of these instruments. Marketable securities and cash equivalents, which consist of money market funds, are measured and recorded at fair value on the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated balance sheets using Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs. The Company determined the fair value of its Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> financial instruments, which are traded in active markets, using quoted market prices for identical instruments. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transfers between Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> and Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> or transfers in or out of Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> during the periods ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The following table summarizes the fair value hierarchy of financial assets measured at fair value as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;(in thousands):</p>
   <p style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em> Income Taxes</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company recorded an income tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944079" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">14.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million on the pretax loss of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944080" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">57.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The income tax benefit (expense) consisted primarily of tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944081" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="djco:IncomeTaxReconciliationRealizedGainsOnMarketableSecurities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">15.8</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;related to unrealized losses on marketable securities, and tax expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944082" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationIncomeTaxExpenseBenefitAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;on income from US operations and dividend income. Consequently, the overall effective tax rate for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145944084" contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">25.3</ix:nonFraction>%, after including the taxes on the unrealized losses on marketable securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, the Company recorded an income tax provision of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944086" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million on pretax income of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944087" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">76.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The income tax provision consisted of tax provisions of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944088" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="djco:IncomeTaxReconciliationRealizedGainsOnMarketableSecurities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">19.2</ix:nonFraction> million on the unrealized gains on marketable securities, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944089" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationIncomeTaxExpenseBenefitAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.9</ix:nonFraction> million on income from US operations and dividend income, and a tax provision of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944090" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationStateAndLocalIncomeTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million for the effect of a change in state apportionment on the beginning of the year&#8217;s deferred tax liability. These tax liabilities were partially offset by a tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145944091" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationDeductionsDividends" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million for the dividends received deduction and other permanent book and tax differences. Consequently, the overall effective tax rate for the <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025 </em>was <ix:nonFraction id="c145944093" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">27</ix:nonFraction>%, after including the taxes on the unrealized gains on marketable securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company files consolidated federal income tax returns, with its domestic subsidiary, in the United States and with various state jurisdictions and is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer subject to examinations for fiscal years before fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;with regard to federal income taxes and fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>&#160;for state income taxes.&#160; The Canadian subsidiary files a federal and provincial tax return in Canada.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Stock-Based Compensation</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company has implemented <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> equity incentive plans, <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> for key employees and <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> for non-employee directors, each providing for the grant of incentive stock options, non-qualified stock options, restricted stock units (RSUs), and other equity-based awards.&#160; As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c145944103" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_PlanNameAxis-EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,920</ix:nonFraction> shares available for future grants under the key employee&#8217;s equity incentive plan, which authorizes the issuance of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c145944104" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_PlanNameAxis-EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,720</ix:nonFraction> shares. Under the non-employee director plan, which authorizes the issuance of <ix:nonFraction id="c145944105" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_PlanNameAxis-NonEmployeeDirectorPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c145944106" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_PlanNameAxis-NonEmployeeDirectorPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,655</ix:nonFraction> shares available for grants as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. The Company has generally issued restricted stock units that vest ratably over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145944107">two</span> years of continuous service from the grant date and, upon vesting, are issued from the Company&#8217;s treasury shares. The Company accounts for share-based compensation utilizing the fair value recognition requirement pursuant to <i>ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> Compensation</i>&#8212;<i>Stock Compensation.</i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For its restricted stock units, the Company uses the closed market price on the date of grant as the fair market value of the stock. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> historically paid any cash dividends on its common stock and as a result does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reduce the grant-date fair value per share by the present value of dividends expected to be paid during the requisite service period for restricted stock units. Share based compensation awards are expensed on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods, which are generally the vesting periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company will recognize the effect of awards for which the requisite service period is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> rendered when the award is forfeited. That is, the Company recognizes the effect of forfeitures in compensation cost when they occur. Previously recognized compensation cost for an award is reversed in the period the award is forfeited.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">8.</em> Commitments and Contingencies</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">From time to time, the Company is subject to litigation arising in the normal course of its business. While it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> possible to predict the results of such litigation, management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe the ultimate outcome of these matters will have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Net Income (Loss) Per Share</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Basic net income (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net income (loss) per share is computed using the treasury stock method by dividing net income (loss) by the weighted average number of dilutive common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted shares outstanding is calculated by adding to the weighted average shares outstanding any potential dilutive securities outstanding for the period. Potential dilutive securities for the Company include only unvested restricted stock units, which have been excluded from the calculation of diluted net loss per share for the periods presented because including them would have been antidilutive. Accordingly, basic and diluted net income (loss) per share are equal for these periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s basic and diluted net income (loss) per share was as follows (in thousands, except share and per share amounts):</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-10-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3202833" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> Segments Information</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The key factors used to identify the reportable segments are the organization of the Company&#8217;s businesses and alignment of its internal operations. Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise for which discrete financial information is available and evaluated regularly by the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;), in deciding how to allocate resources and assess performance.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, serving as the CODM, reviews consolidated financial data to allocate resources and assess performance. The CODM focuses on consolidated net income (loss) from the condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss), comparing results with prior periods, forecasts, and relevant expenditure categories for each segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

Accordingly, Traditional Business revenues are comprised of advertising, circulation, and advertising service fees and other, while Journal Technologies revenues are comprised of licensing and maintenance fees, consulting fees, and other public service fees. All inter-segment transactions were eliminated. Corporate is presented below as a non-operating segment to reconcile segment results to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statement line-item totals.   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><a href="#"></a><a id="mda" href="#"></a><b>Item 2. Management</b>&#8217;<b>s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 44pt;text-indent:-44pt;"><b>Results of Operations</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company continues to operate as two different businesses: (1) The Traditional Business, being the business of newspaper publishing and related services that the Company had before 1999 when it purchased a software development company, and (2) Journal Technologies, Inc. (&#8220;Journal Technologies&#8221;), a wholly-owned subsidiary which supplies case management software systems and related products to courts, prosecutor and public defender offices, probation departments and other justice agencies, including administrative law organizations, city and county governments and bar associations. These organizations use the Journal Technologies family of products to help manage cases and information electronically, to interface with other critical justice partners and to extend electronic services to the public, including e-filing and a website to pay traffic citations and fees online. These products are licensed or subscribed to in approximately 37 states and internationally.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Reportable Segments</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

All inter-segment transactions were eliminated. Additional details about each of the reportable segments and the Company&#8217;s corporate income and expenses for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, are set forth below (in thousands):</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Consolidated Financials Comparison</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Consolidated revenues were $42.3&#160;million and $35.9&#160;million for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This&#160;increase&#160; of $6.4&#160;million (17.8%) was primarily from increases in (i) Journal Technologies&#8217; other public service fees of $2.2&#160;million, license and maintenance fees of $2.0&#160;million, and consulting fees of $1.8&#160;million, and (ii) the Traditional Business&#8217; advertising revenues of $0.3&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Approximately&#160;79%&#160;and&#160;76%&#160;of our revenues during the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025&#160;were derived from Journal Technologies. In addition, our revenues during the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026&#160;were primarily from the United States, with approximately $3.3&#160;million (7.9%) from foreign countries. Almost all of Journal Technologies&#8217; revenues are from governmental agencies.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Consolidated operating expenses&#160;increased by $4.6&#160;million (13.5%) to $38.8&#160;million from $34.2&#160;million. Total salaries and employee benefits&#160;increased by $1.8&#160;million (7.6%) to $26.0&#160;million from $&#160;24.2&#160;million primarily due to annual salary adjustments and the hiring of additional staff members to strengthen operational efficiencies, conduct product development and address technical debt, and bolster teams working on our installation projects. Outside services&#160;increased by $0.7&#160;million (19.4%) to $4.3&#160;million from $3.6&#160;million mainly because of additional contractor services and increased third-party hosting fees which were billed to clients. Other general and administrative expenses&#160;increased by $2.6&#160;million (93.6%) to $5.4&#160;million from $2.8&#160;million, primarily driven by a $1.5 million increase in accounting and legal fees, including higher accounting costs associated with efforts to remediate previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting and higher legal and service provider expenses related to proxy solicitation and stockholder outreach activities, as well as a $0.4 million increase in costs related to the adoption and implementation of software and related process changes supporting the Company&#8217;s modernization initiatives. The Company expects these costs to remain elevated in the near term as these initiatives continue</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Other income (expense) for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026&#160;decreased by $135.0&#160;million, resulting in $60.6&#160;million of other expense, compared with $74.5&#160;million of other income for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025. This change was primarily driven by unrealized losses on marketable securities of $62.9&#160;million, compared with unrealized gains of $72.8&#160;million in the prior-year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, consolidated pretax loss was $57.1&#160;million and pretax income was $76.2&#160;million, respectively, and consolidated net loss was $42.6&#160;million and net income was $55.6&#160;million, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">As of&#160;March 31, 2026, the aggregate fair market value of the Company&#8217;s marketable securities was $430.1&#160;million. These securities had approximately&#160;$291.0&#160;million of cumulative unrealized gains before estimated taxes of $75.7&#160;million. Most of the unrealized gains were in the common stocks of three U.S. financial institutions and one foreign manufacturer.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Taxes</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026, the Company recorded an income tax benefit of $14.5&#160;million on the pretax loss of $57.1&#160;million. The income tax benefit and expense consisted primarily of tax benefit of $15.8 million&#160;related to unrealized losses on marketable securities, and tax expense of $1.4 million&#160;on income from US operations and dividend income. Consequently, the overall effective tax rate for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026&#160;was&#160;25.3% after including the taxes on the unrealized gains on marketable securities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025, the Company recorded an income tax provision of $20.6&#160;million on pretax income of $76.2&#160;million. The income tax provision consisted of $19.2 million related to unrealized gains on marketable securities, $0.9 million related to income from U.S. operations and dividend income, and a tax provision of $0.6 million for the effect of a change in state apportionment on the beginning of the year&#8217;s deferred tax liability. These tax liabilities were partially offset by a tax benefit of $0.1 million for the dividends received deduction and other permanent book and tax differences. Consequently, the overall effective tax rate for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025&#160;was 27%, after including the taxes on the unrealized gains on marketable securities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company files consolidated federal income tax returns, with its domestic subsidiary, in the United States and with various state jurisdictions and is no longer subject to examinations for fiscal years before fiscal year 2021 with regard to federal income taxes and fiscal year 2020 for state income taxes.&#160; The Canadian subsidiary files a federal and provincial tax return in Canada.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Journal Technologies</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026, Journal Technologies&#8217; pretax income&#160;increased by $3.7&#160;million to $4.2&#160;million, compared to $0.5&#160;million for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025. The&#160;increase&#160;was primarily attributable to&#160;higher&#160;revenues of $6.0&#160;million, partially offset by&#160;increased operating expenses of $2.3&#160;million.</p>

Licensing and maintenance fees&#160;increased by $2.0&#160;million (13.4%) to $17.0&#160;million, while other public service fees&#160;increased by $2.2&#160;million (30.8%) to $9.3&#160;million, primarily due to increased e-filing revenues. Consulting fees&#160;increased by $1.8&#160;million (34.4%) to $7.1&#160;million, primarily due to the timing of project go-lives and deferred revenue recognition.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Traditional Business</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026, the Traditional Business reported a pretax loss of $1.1&#160;million, compared to pretax income of $1.2&#160;million for the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025. This decrease was primarily attributable to increased accounting and consulting fees and other operating expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Total revenues&#160;increased by $0.4&#160;million (4.2%) to $8.8&#160;million from $8.5&#160;million in the prior-year period. Advertising revenues&#160;increased by $0.3&#160;million (4.7%) to $6.6&#160;million, while circulation revenues&#160;increased by $0.1&#160;million (2.8%&#160;).</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Daily Journals accounted for approximately 95% of the Traditional Business&#8217; total circulation revenues, which remained consistent year-over-year.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Traditional Business segment operating expenses&#160;increased by $2.6&#160;million (36.0%) to $9.9&#160;million from $7.3&#160;million, primarily resulting from increased personnel costs, merchant discount fees, additional promotional expenses, and accounting advisory fees primarily associated with the remediation of material weaknesses in our internal controls and higher legal and service provider expenses associated with proxy solicitation and stockholder outreach activities.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Consolidated Financials Comparison</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Consolidated revenues were $22.7&#160;million and $18.2&#160;million for three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This increase of $4.5&#160;million (25.0%) was primarily from increases in (i) Journal Technologies&#8217; consulting fees of $2.3&#160;million, other public service fees of $1.2&#160;million, and license and maintenance fees of $1.0&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Approximately&#160;80%&#160;and&#160;76%&#160;of our revenues during the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 and 2025&#160;were derived from Journal Technologies. In addition, our revenues during the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;were primarily from the United States, with approximately $2.2&#160;million (9.7%) from foreign countries.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Consolidated operating expenses&#160;increased by $2.5&#160;million (14.6%) to $19.7&#160;million from $17.2&#160;million. Total salaries and employee benefits&#160;increased by $0.7&#160;million (6.1%) to $13.1&#160;million from $12.3&#160;million primarily due to annual salary adjustments and the hiring of additional staff members to strengthen operational efficiencies, conduct product development and address technical debt, and bolster teams working on our installation projects. Outside services&#160;decreased by $0.1&#160;million (3.7%) to $1.7&#160;million from $1.8&#160;million. Other general and administrative expenses&#160;increased by $2.0&#160;million (147.6%) to $3.4&#160;million from $1.4&#160;million, primarily due to higher accounting and consulting fees associated with remediation of material weaknesses in internal controls.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Other expenses for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;was $50.0&#160;million of other expense, compared with $60.3&#160;million of other income for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2025. This change was primarily driven by unrealized losses on marketable securities of $51.2&#160;million, compared with unrealized gains of $59.4&#160;million in the prior-year quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 and 2025, consolidated pretax loss was $47.0&#160;million and pretax income was $61.3&#160;million, respectively, and consolidated net loss was $34.6&#160;million and net income was $44.7&#160;million, respectively.</p>
