  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Journal Technologies</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026, Journal Technologies&#8217; pretax income was $3.1&#160;million compared to $0.1&#160;million for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2025. The&#160;increase&#160;was primarily attributable to higher revenues of $4.4&#160;million, partially offset by&#160;increased operating expenses of $1.4&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Revenues increased by $4.4&#160;million (32.2%) to $18.2&#160;million from $13.8&#160;million during the prior-year quarter. Licensing and maintenance fees&#160;increased by $1.0&#160;million (13.7%) to $8.5&#160;million, while other public service fees&#160;increased by $1.2&#160;million (32.0%) to $4.8&#160;million, primarily due to increased e-filing revenues. Consulting fees&#160;increased by $2.3&#160;million (84.5%) to $4.9&#160;million, primarily due to the timing of project go-lives and deferred revenue recognition.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Operating expenses&#160;increased by $1.4&#160;million (10.2%) to $15.1&#160;million, primarily due to increased personnel costs, higher contractor utilization, and increased hosting costs billed to customers.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Traditional Business</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026, the Traditional Business reported a pretax loss of $0.5&#160;million, compared to pretax income of $0.9&#160;million for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2025. This&#160;decrease&#160;was primarily attributable to other operating expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Total revenues&#160;increased by $0.1&#160;million (2.3%) to $4.5&#160;million from $4.4&#160;million in the prior-year quarter. Advertising and circulation revenues&#160;increased by $0.1&#160;million (5.3%&#160;).</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Traditional Business segment operating expenses&#160;increased by $1.5&#160;million (42.0%) to $5.0&#160;million from $3.5&#160;million, primarily resulting from increased merchant discount fees, additional promotional expenses, and accounting advisory fees primarily associated with the remediation of material weaknesses in our internal controls, as well as higher legal and service provider expenses associated with proxy solicitation and stockholder outreach activities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Liquidity and Capital Resources</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026,&#160;our cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities&#160;decreased by $62.8&#160;million, reflecting net pretax unrealized losses on marketable securities of $62.9&#160;million. The investments in marketable securities, which had an adjusted cost basis of approximately $139.1 million and a market value of approximately $430.1&#160;million as of&#160;March 31, 2026, generated approximately $2.6&#160;million in dividends and interest income during the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026. These securities had approximately&#160;$291.0&#160;million of cumulative unrealized gains before estimated taxes of $75.7&#160;million which will become due only when we sell securities in which there is realized appreciation.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">No marketable securities were sold during the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026. The margin loan principal balance was paid down by $2.0 million using excess cash from operations. The loan balance was $20.0&#160;million and $22.0&#160;million as of&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;September 30, 2025, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">As of&#160;March 31, 2026, we had working capital of $441.7&#160;million, including the liabilities for deferred revenue of $16.4&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We believe that we will be able to fund our operations for the foreseeable future through our cash flows from operations and our current working capital, and we expect that any such cash flows will be invested in our businesses. We may or may not have the ability to borrow additional amounts against our marketable securities and, among other possibilities, we may be required to consider selling securities to generate cash if needed to fund ongoing operations. The amount available for borrowing is based on the market value of our investment portfolio and fluctuates depending on the value of the underlying securities. In addition, we could be subject to margin calls should the value of the investments decrease significantly.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Operating Activities</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $2.2&#160;million. Cash provided by operating activities consisted of a net loss of $42.6&#160;million, adjusted for non-cash items of $48.3&#160;million, and cash used for working capital of $3.5&#160;million. Adjustments for non-cash items consisted primarily of $62.9&#160;million of net unrealized losses on marketable securities, and $14.8&#160;million of deferred income tax benefit. The use of cash from changes in operating assets and liabilities was primarily attributable to a $7.7&#160;million&#160;decrease&#160;in accrued liabilities, including non-qualified deferred compensation, $0.6&#160;million decrease in income taxes payable, $1.9&#160;million&#160;decrease&#160;in deferred revenue, and $1.3&#160;million&#160;increase&#160;in prepaid expenses and other assets, partially offset by a $7.4&#160;million&#160;decrease&#160;in accounts receivable, reflecting improved collections, and a $0.7&#160;million&#160;increase&#160;in accounts payable.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">For the&#160;six months ended March 31, 2025, net cash provided by operating activities was $1.6 million. Cash provided by operating activities consisted of net income of $55.6 million, adjusted for non-cash items of $52.3 million, and cash used for working capital of $1.6 million. Adjustments for non-cash items consisted primarily of $72.8 million of net unrealized gains on marketable securities, partially offset by $20.3 million of deferred income tax expense, as well as $0.1 million of depreciation and amortization and $0.1 million of stock-based compensation. The use of cash from changes in operating assets and liabilities was primarily attributable to a $6.5 million decrease in deferred revenue and a $2.5 million decrease in accrued liabilities, including non-qualified deferred compensation, partially offset by a $7.4 million decrease in accounts receivable, reflecting improved collections.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><a href="#"></a><a id="quantitative" href="#"></a><b>Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</b> </p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">We are a smaller reporting company as defined by Rule 12b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), and are not required to provide the information required under this item.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><a href="#"></a><a id="controls" href="#"></a><b>Item 4. Controls and Procedures</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;"><i><b>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s management, with the participation of the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer (Principal Financial and Accounting Officer), evaluated the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures, as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act as of March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">As previously disclosed in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, management identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting related to (i) segregation of duties and (ii) revenue recognition.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">Based on this evaluation, and in light of these material weaknesses, management concluded that the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of&#160;March 31, 2026. However, management has made substantial progress in remediation. While the Company believes that the material weaknesses have been addressed through the actions described below, it must see sustained operating effectiveness over a sufficient period before concluding and declaring that the weaknesses have been fully remediated.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;"><i><b>Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">During the quarter ended&#160;March 31, 2026, the Company continued to execute its remediation plan and made significant progress building on its prior actions. Specifically, the Company:</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table style="border-collapse:collapse;height:auto;width:100%;">

     <td style="padding:0;vertical-align:top;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Completed the implementation of enhancements to its enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, strengthening system-enforced segregation of duties, user access governance, and workflow approval controls, and expanding their consistent application across financial reporting processes.</p></td>
